key_insight: CareConnect shows that a tightly scoped LLM agent can automate healthcare scheduling and information lookup with strong safety guardrails, without providing medical advice.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce administrative burden and improve access by helping patients book, modify, or cancel appointments while keeping unsafe medical queries out of scope.
method: Built a conversational agent with LLM function calling and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Integrated eight domain-specific tools for scheduling and facility information tasks
Added deterministic safety guardrails, including emergency detection and medical-intent refusal
evidence_signal: In testing across 680 task-oriented scenarios, the system achieved 91.8% task completion, 96.0% safety compliance on safety-critical cases, 2.2-second median latency, and $0.0324 average cost per appointment.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will need careful integration with legacy healthcare systems and ongoing monitoring to ensure safety rules remain effective as workflows and user behavior change.
paper_title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
